land.text: Ceredigion and Ystrad Tywi, 'the former Kingdom of Ceredigion plus the region known as Ystrad Tywi'

predecessors.note: Seisyllwg page infobox: 'Changed name from Ceredigion: 680'. Rhodri Mawr became steward over Gwgon's realm after Gwgon drowned in 872 and installed his son Cadell; Rhodri was 'slain in battle by the forces of Ceolwulf II of Mercia in 878' (Rhodri page). The Gwynedd dossier records the matching loss in 878, when Cliopatria's Seisyllwg row begins.

land.text: Seisyllwg with Dyfed: 'In 920 Hywel merged Seisyllwg with the Kingdom of Dyfed to form the new kingdom of Deheubarth'

successors.note: Cliopatria keeps the Seisyllwg row to 959 and grows it over Gwynedd (922) and Powys (947); those shapes belong to Deheubarth, Gwynedd and Powys in the dossiers of those states.

keyframe_review.note: 4,512 km2 (resolves to 16 cells): Ceredigion (5 cells) and the north of Carmarthenshire (6 cells), Ystrad Tywi. Seisyllwg page: 'consisted of the former Kingdom of Ceredigion plus the region known as Ystrad Tywi'. The page gives no capital and no area.

correction.text: the 878 shape: Ceredigion and Ystrad Tywi without Powys, valid 900-904

keyframe_review.note: 8,914 km2: +21 cells (5.3 thousand km2) that are exactly Cliopatria's Kingdom of Powys cells, a row it leaves empty for 900-910. The Cadell page does not mention Powys for Cadell ('Powys appears only in a possible installation of his brother Merfyn'), and the Powys dossier draws Powys as its own kingdom under Llywelyn ap Merfyn through those years. The land should stay Powys's; Seisyllwg keeps its 878 shape until Dyfed is added (905).

correction.text: Seisyllwg with Dyfed: the 911 shape applied from 905

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 905-910: the 878 shape plus Dyfed. Cadell page: 'Cadell and Hywel together also conquered Dyfed in 904-905'; Hywel page: no king of Dyfed is recorded after Llywarch ap Hyfaidd died in 904 and Hywel 'probably gained Dyfed through his marriage to Llywarch's heir, Elen' (infobox: Dyfed from 904, succession box 905). Cliopatria adds the ten Dyfed cells only in 911.

correction.text: Seisyllwg with Dyfed, under Hywel and Clydog; valid to 919, from 920 it is Deheubarth

keyframe_review.note: 7,871 km2 (cell count 6,578 km2): the Seisyllwg-and-Dyfed shape, valid to 919. Cadell dies in 909 (Cadell and Hywel Dda pages; the Seisyllwg page says 911) and his lands go to Hywel and Clydog, who 'jointly submitted to Edward the Elder' in 918 (Hywel page). 'In 920 Hywel merged Seisyllwg with the Kingdom of Dyfed to form the new kingdom of Deheubarth' (Seisyllwg page); Cliopatria keeps the Seisyllwg row, so the shape stops being Seisyllwg's in 920.

correction.text: the Seisyllwg-and-Dyfed land, which is the kingdom of Deheubarth from 920; the 17 Gwynedd cells belong to Gwynedd until 941

keyframe_review.note: 14,214 km2 (cell count 10.9 thousand km2): the Seisyllwg-and-Dyfed shape plus 17 cells of Cliopatria's Gwynedd shape (Gwynedd, Conwy and Anglesey cells). Hywel took Gwynedd only in 942 ('Idwal Foel and his brother Elisedd were killed fighting Edmund's forces ... Hywel ... took control of Gwynedd', Hywel page). 920-941 the land is Deheubarth's (Seisyllwg plus Dyfed) and Gwynedd's own; the row belongs to the Deheubarth and Gwynedd dossiers, not to Seisyllwg.

correction.text: Seisyllwg with Dyfed only; Hywel's 942-949 Gwynedd and Powys and the split of 950 are Deheubarth's, Gwynedd's and Powys's

keyframe_review.note: 18,353 km2 (cell count 15.7 thousand km2): the previous shape plus 20 cells of Cliopatria's Powys shape. Hywel 'took control of Gwynedd, which probably also gave him Powys' (942, no month) and died in 949 or 950, when 'Gwynedd went to Idwal Foel's sons, Iago and Ieuaf' and 'Deheubarth and Powys were divided among Owain, Rhodri, and Edwin'. 942-949 the land is Hywel's Deheubarth; after 950 it is split. Not Seisyllwg's: Seisyllwg ended in 920.

region.text: Ceredigion and Ystrad Tywi, the kingdom of Seisyllwg

ledger.note: 878: Rhodri Mawr is killed and Cadell holds Ceredigion and Ystrad Tywi as the kingdom of Seisyllwg. Rhodri was 'slain in battle by the forces of Ceolwulf II of Mercia in 878'; Cadell had been installed as king under him after Gwgon of Ceredigion drowned in 872 ('Reign: 872-909', Cadell page). The year of independence is Cliopatria's; no page says Seisyllwg became a separate realm in 878.

region.text: Dyfed: the ten cells (Pembrokeshire, south Carmarthenshire) that Cliopatria adds in 911

ledger.note: 904-905: Cadell and Hywel conquer Dyfed. 'Cadell and Hywel together also conquered Dyfed in 904-905' (Cadell page); the Hywel page has Hywel gain Dyfed 'probably' through his marriage to Elen, heiress of Llywarch ap Hyfaidd (died 904). Cliopatria adds the land only in 911.

909: Cadell dies and Hywel and Clydog share the kingdom. 'Cadell left his territorial holdings to his sons Hywel and Clydog on his death in 909' (the Seisyllwg page says 'After Cadell's death in 911, Seisyllwg was divided among his two sons'). The brothers 'jointly submitted to Edward the Elder' in 918 (Hywel page). Same state and colour.

region.text: Seisyllwg and Dyfed, united as Deheubarth

ledger.note: 920: Seisyllwg becomes Deheubarth. 'In 920 Hywel merged Seisyllwg with the Kingdom of Dyfed to form the new kingdom of Deheubarth'; Clydog died in 920 leaving the realm to Hywel (Hywel page). Infobox: 'Union with Dyfed forming Deheubarth: 920'.

wars.name: Cadell and Hywel's conquest of Dyfed

zones.text: Dyfed: the ten cells (Pembrokeshire, south Carmarthenshire) that Cliopatria adds in 911

wars.outcome: Dyfed, without a king after Llywarch ap Hyfaidd's death in 904, passes to Hywel (by marriage, 'probably') and Cadell; the Hywel page gives no battle.
wars.note: The Cadell page says conquered; the Hywel page says probably by marriage to Elen.

wars.name: Hywel and Clydog's submission to Edward the Elder
wars.outcome: Hywel and Clydog 'jointly submitted to Edward the Elder' of England; no land changes hands. The Wessex dossier carries the vassal tint.

certainty.note: No treaty line or survey is dated; the realm is described by its cantrefs (Ceredigion, Ystrad Tywi, later Dyfed), not by boundaries.

notes: Five pages were budgeted and four used. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Seisyllwg row (878-959) is really Seisyllwg to 920 and then Hywel Dda's Deheubarth (the Deheubarth dossier starts 920 with this state as predecessor), so the 922 and 947 shapes are marked wrong and their land belongs to the Deheubarth, Gwynedd and Powys dossiers; the 900-910 shape wrongly swallows Powys. Disagreements between pages: Cadell's death 909 (Cadell and Hywel Dda pages) vs 911 (Seisyllwg page), which is also Cliopatria's 911 shape; Dyfed 904-905 (Cadell and Hywel pages) vs Cliopatria 911; Cadell reign from 872 (page) vs Cliopatria 878; Seisyllwg infobox 'Changed name from Ceredigion: 680'. For the England and Wessex dossiers: their vassal events with counterpart kingdom-of-seisyllwg are 918 (Wessex, Hywel and Clydog), 927 (England, Eamont) and 959 (England, 'Seisyllwg's row ends'); Seisyllwg ended in 920 and its successor is deheubarth, so the 927 and 959 events should name deheubarth, and the 918 tie needs a vassal_end at 920. The Hywel Dda page does not mention Eamont. Capitals: an empty list, because neither the Seisyllwg nor the other pages give a seat. Rulers omitted. Region names: all in the gazetteer. Quotation marks enclose strings the page-fetch tool returned as quotations; other wording paraphrases its summary of the page, which was read by WebFetch only (no raw page text).
